owner.occupation: Board-certified music therapist on a sabbatical year

world.bio: I'm a board-certified music therapist from Vancouver, spending a sabbatical year in Dali. For six years I worked in a hospice and a dementia care unit, mostly with a guitar and a small drum. I came to Yunnan to rest, learn Mandarin and see whether I still like my work when nobody is paying me for it. On weekends I play in the old town for tips.
skills_assets: Board-certified music therapist (MT-BC), six years of clinical work in hospice and dementia care
Session design for older adults: familiar-song groups, rhythm, reminiscence and life-review work
A travel guitar, a frame drum, a small set of tuned percussion and a portable speaker
Clinical documentation habits: SOAP notes, goal tracking, baseline and follow-up observations
Beginner Mandarin, picking up a few words of Bai from market vendors

projects.name: Credential maintenance
projects.text: My certification requires continuing education and a minimum number of clinical contact hours in the five-year cycle. I'm about a hundred supervised hours short of where I should be by next summer, because the sabbatical took me out of practice. I have emailed two clinics in Kunming and one hospital in Dali with no reply.

projects.name: Mandarin tutoring
projects.text: Twice a week with a patient tutor named Ms. Yang. We started with greetings and have worked up to ordering at the noodle shop without pointing.

projects.name: Old-town busking
projects.text: Saturday afternoons by the bridge. I earn about eighty to a hundred yuan, which pays for the guitar strings and one decent lunch.

projects.name: Dali clinical placement search
projects.text: Reached out to a Dali hospital, two nursing homes and a Kunming clinic. Two say they can't take a foreign trainee, one wants Mandarin fluency, one never replied. Considering a remote supervisor from Vancouver, but the board wants in-person contact hours.

notes.text: Woke up before six to the sound of someone chanting next door. Made coffee. The mountains looked like a postcard and I resented it a little. I think I came here to run away from something and I'm not sure what.

Emailed the third clinic. I explained I'm board-certified, fluent in English, a beginner in Mandarin and zero in Bai, and that I need supervised hours. No reply yet. Everyone is polite but nobody has a space where a music therapist can sit for twenty hours a month.
Mandarin lesson. I said 'I want to eat the bridge' instead of 'I want to cross the bridge'. Ms. Yang laughed so hard she had to put her tea down. I wrote the right word on my hand.

Mum called. She is moving into a condo in Burnaby and wants me to decide what to do with my old room. I said throw out the posters. She said she'd keep the guitar case. We both got a bit teary and pretended it was the connection.
Visa extension paperwork. Three trips to the exit-entry office. The officer was kind and the photocopier was not. I now own forty-one passport photos.

Busked by the bridge. An old Bai woman stopped and listened to 'You Are My Sunshine' with her eyes closed. When I finished she said something I didn't understand and pressed a pear into my hand. I ate it on the way home and cried a little because it was the best pear.

Reread my last clinical notes from Vancouver, the ones on a client with advanced dementia who woke up when I sang a hymn from her childhood. I wrote 'the right song is a door.' I haven't opened a door like that in nine months and I miss it more than I thought.

Long walk around Erhai. I don't want to be the person who takes a year off and comes back deskilled. But I also don't want to apologise for resting. I'm trying to hold both. It is very tiring to hold both.

messages.text:
Mum: Do you want your skates?
Me: Keep them.
Mum: Are you eating?
Me: Noodles. Every day. Don't worry.

Ms. Yang: 你今天说得很好。
Me: Xie xie.
Ms. Yang: 下次我们练习医院里的词。
Me: Hospital words. Yes please.

Priya: Are you coming back in July?
Me: That's the plan.
Priya: Your caseload is waiting.
Me: I need clinical hours before then, and I can't find a placement here.

Jonas: Want to come to the market? There's a guy who sells old cassette tapes.
Me: Old Bai music?
Jonas: I think so. He had a whole wall.
Me: I'll come.

Jonas: Found the cassette guy again. Whole wall of Bai folk tapes, he said nobody buys them.
Me: Can he play them?
Jonas: He has two working players. Come see.

relations.about: Moving into a condo in Burnaby and sorting out a lifetime of boxes
Former hospice colleague, covering her caseload

constraints: Cannot legally work for pay on a tourist-type visa
Supervised hours must be with an approved supervisor and documented
sensitive: Quietly worried her skills will go stale and the sabbatical will cost her her credential
Not sure she wants to return to hospice work at all
